suite.name: Composed assistant end-to-end suite (mock)
suite.description: Offline end-to-end fixture for the composed assistant. It runs the nested coding graph and the storyteller through the real runtime, grades the exit artifact, and derives best-single, cheapest, oracle, and random-routing baselines from the same cases. One case is a deliberate routing loss and one is a deliberate validity failure so the report includes failure slices.

limitations: The mock provider serves scripted responses; these metrics validate the harness and suite, not model quality.
Small suite (n=5); treat this as a development smoke result, not a quality claim.
Wall-clock latency includes harness overhead and varies between runs; it is excluded from the determinism fingerprint.

Best-single and cheapest-capable baselines run each worker node directly on the full task. They exclude routing and handoff, which is the point of the comparison, but they also ignore the graph's node view and any intermediate artifacts.
Oracle labels force only the first router's branch. Nested routing is measured through the case's authored mock scripts or live provider behavior, not exhaustively labeled.
Oracle labeling runs every selected case; stratification is the suite author's selection (tags/limit), not an automatic sample design.
Costs come from manifest pricing. Free local model manifests report zero marginal cost, so a cost band can collapse to a single $0 point.
Measured oracle labels are produced by the same checks used for the graph, so a broken check under-labels every branch equally.
No incumbent report was supplied, so the incumbent baseline is unavailable.
profile override max_steps=8 ignored because it raises the graph default 6; pass --allow-budget-override to apply it

labeling.ambiguity_rule: Mark a case ambiguous when the best and second-best measured branch qualities differ by at most oracle_ambiguity_delta, or when the case explicitly says so.
labeling.notes: Labels are produced by running the graph with the first router forced through each candidate branch and grading the same exit checks. Nested routing follows the case's scripted decisions.

e2e.baseline_notes: Every example model manifest is free, so cost bands collapse to a $0 point; quality is scripted task success, not a model-quality claim.

pareto.notes: Quality is task success; cost is manifest-priced cost per task. Frontier entries are not dominated on quality and cost. With free local manifests every configuration sits in the same $0 cost band, so the highest-quality configuration wins that band. Do not compare configurations at different budgets and call the difference quality.
